meta.description: Provide administrators with a paginated list of all system users, allowing them to select a user for update or deletion.
meta.process_description: This program retrieves and displays all registered users from the User Security file (USRSEC) in a paginated list of up to 10 users per screen, enabling administrators to browse the full user population. Administrators can navigate forward (PF8) and backward (PF7) through pages of users, or search by entering a specific User ID to position the list. For each displayed user, the administrator can enter a selection code ('U' to update or 'D' to delete) next to a user record, which transfers control to the appropriate maintenance program (COUSR02C for update, COUSR03C for delete). The program is accessible only to authenticated admin users, returning unauthenticated sessions to the sign-on screen and returning authenticated admins to the admin menu (COADM01C) on PF3.

files.USRSEC: User Security file storing all system user accounts including user ID, name, and user type (admin/regular)

business_rules: Only authenticated administrator sessions may access this program; unauthenticated users are redirected to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C).
A maximum of 10 user records are displayed per page.
Valid selection actions are 'U' (Update) and 'D' (Delete) only; any other selection code is rejected with an error message.
Only one user may be selected for action at a time per screen interaction.
Administrators cannot navigate before the first page (PF7 blocked at page 1) or beyond the last page (PF8 blocked when no further records exist).
Selecting 'U' transfers control to COUSR02C (user update program); selecting 'D' transfers control to COUSR03C (user delete program).
PF3 returns the administrator to the admin main menu (COADM01C) without performing any user action.
An optional User ID search field allows the administrator to position the list starting from a specific user, enabling direct navigation within a large user population.

variables.name: WS-VARIABLES
variables.description: Group record holding all general working-storage variables used during the user list administration process, such as program identity, error tracking, and pagination state.

variables.name: WS-PGMNAME
variables.description: The internal name of this program (COUSR00C), used when passing control to other programs or logging, so the system knows which program is currently executing the user list function.

variables.name: WS-TRANID
variables.description: The CICS transaction identifier (CU00) associated with the user list screen. This is the transaction code an administrator invokes to access the user management list, and it is displayed on-screen for reference.

variables.name: WS-MESSAGE
variables.description: The message displayed at the bottom of the user list screen to communicate feedback to the administrator, such as validation errors (invalid selection code), navigation boundary warnings (already on first/last page), or confirmation of actions taken.

variables.name: WS-USRSEC-FILE
variables.description: The name of the User Security file (USRSEC) that stores all system user accounts. This value is used when opening, reading, or positioning within the file to retrieve the list of users displayed to the administrator.

variables.name: WS-ERR-FLG
variables.description: An error indicator flag that tracks whether a business or validation error has occurred during the current screen interaction (e.g., invalid selection code, no user selected). When set to 'Y', the screen is redisplayed with an error message rather than proceeding with the requested action.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-ON
variables.description: Condition name indicating that an error has been detected during the administrator's interaction with the user list screen, causing the program to halt the requested action and display an appropriate error message.

variables.name: ERR-FLG-OFF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that no error has been detected and the administrator's requested action (navigation, selection, or search) can proceed normally.

variables.name: WS-USER-SEC-EOF
variables.description: An end-of-file indicator for the User Security file. When set to 'Y', it signals that all user records have been read and there are no more users to retrieve, which determines whether a next page of users exists and controls the PF8 (forward navigation) availability.

variables.name: USER-SEC-EOF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the end of the User Security file has been reached, meaning all user accounts have been read and no further pages of users are available for the administrator to browse.

variables.name: USER-SEC-NOT-EOF
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the User Security file still has more user records beyond those currently displayed, meaning additional pages are available for the administrator to navigate forward.

variables.name: WS-SEND-ERASE-FLG
variables.description: A screen-send control flag that determines whether the user list screen should be fully erased and redrawn (ERASE option) when sent to the administrator's terminal. 'Y' causes a full screen refresh, typically used on first display; 'N' allows a partial update for subsequent interactions.

variables.name: SEND-ERASE-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating the user list screen should be completely cleared and redrawn on the administrator's terminal, used when first presenting the screen or after a major navigation event.

variables.name: SEND-ERASE-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating the user list screen should be sent without erasing the existing display, used for partial screen updates during repeated interactions on the same page.

variables.name: WS-RESP-CD
variables.description: The CICS response code returned after each file or system operation (e.g., reading the User Security file). Used to detect whether an operation succeeded or failed, enabling the program to handle errors such as a user record not being found.

variables.name: WS-REAS-CD
variables.description: The CICS reason code providing additional detail about the outcome of a file or system operation, used alongside the response code to diagnose specific error conditions when accessing the User Security file.

variables.name: WS-REC-COUNT
variables.description: A counter tracking how many user records have been retrieved and populated on the current page of the user list. This count (maximum 10) determines how many rows are displayed to the administrator and whether the page is full.

variables.name: WS-IDX
variables.description: A loop index used internally when iterating through the up to 10 user records on the current page, for example when populating the screen rows with user data or scanning for the administrator's selection.

variables.name: WS-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: A working-storage page counter used during pagination processing to calculate and track which page of the user list is being assembled or navigated to, before the final page number is committed to the communication area for display.

variables.name: WS-USER-DATA
variables.description: Group record holding the data for all user accounts displayed on the current page of the user list screen, structured as an array of up to 10 user rows.

variables.name: USER-REC
variables.description: A single row in the user list screen, representing one user account. Up to 10 of these rows are displayed per page, each containing the selection field, user ID, full name, and user type for one system user.

variables.name: USER-SEL
variables.description: The action code entered by the administrator next to a specific user row on the list screen. Valid values are 'U' to update the user's details or 'D' to delete the user account. Any other value is rejected with an error message.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Spacing filler between the selection code and the user ID columns in the user list row, used purely for screen layout alignment and not carrying any business data.

variables.name: USER-ID
variables.description: The unique login identifier of a system user displayed in this row of the user list. The administrator uses this to identify which user account they wish to update or delete.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Spacing filler between the user ID and user name columns in the user list row, used purely for screen layout alignment and not carrying any business data.

variables.name: USER-NAME
variables.description: The full name of the system user displayed in this row of the user list, helping the administrator visually identify the person associated with a user account before selecting it for update or deletion.

variables.name: FILLER
variables.description: Spacing filler between the user name and user type columns in the user list row, used purely for screen layout alignment and not carrying any business data.

variables.name: USER-TYPE
variables.description: The classification of the user account shown in this row, indicating whether the user holds administrator privileges or is a regular user. This helps the administrator understand the access level of each account before taking action.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU00-INFO
variables.description: Group record within the communication area holding all pagination and selection state for the user list screen, passed between program invocations so the administrator's current position and selection are preserved across interactions.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST
variables.description: The user ID of the first user record displayed on the current page of the list. This acts as the backward pagination anchor: when the administrator presses PF7 to go to the previous page, the program uses this value to reposition the User Security file and retrieve the preceding set of users.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST
variables.description: The user ID of the last user record displayed on the current page of the list. This acts as the forward pagination anchor: when the administrator presses PF8 to go to the next page, the program uses this value to reposition the User Security file and retrieve the next set of users.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM
variables.description: The current page number being displayed in the user list, shown on-screen so the administrator knows their position within the full user population. Also used to enforce the business rule that navigation before page 1 is not permitted.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU00-NEXT-PAGE-FLG
variables.description: An indicator of whether additional user records exist beyond the current page. When 'Y', the PF8 (next page) key is enabled; when 'N', the administrator has reached the last page and forward navigation is blocked per business rules.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-YES
variables.description: Condition name indicating that more user accounts exist beyond the current page, allowing the administrator to press PF8 to navigate forward to the next page of users.

variables.name: NEXT-PAGE-NO
variables.description: Condition name indicating that the current page is the last page of users, so PF8 (forward navigation) is blocked and the administrator cannot navigate beyond this point.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG
variables.description: The action code entered by the administrator for the selected user, carried in the communication area between program calls. 'U' routes to the user update program (COUSR02C) and 'D' routes to the user delete program (COUSR03C); any other value is rejected as invalid.

variables.name: CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED
variables.description: The user ID of the specific user account the administrator has chosen to act upon (update or delete). This value is passed in the communication area to the target program (COUSR02C or COUSR03C) so it knows which user record to process.

variables.name: DFHCOMMAREA
variables.description: The CICS communication area passed into this program from the calling program or transaction. It carries context from the previous program interaction, such as the administrator's session credentials and pagination state, enabling the user list program to resume correctly.

variables.name: LK-COMMAREA
variables.description: The raw linkage representation of the communication area data passed into this program. Defined minimally here as a single byte placeholder; the actual structured data (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) is mapped over this area to access the administrator's session information and pagination state.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the central orchestration entry point of the user list program. It determines the session context, authenticates the administrator, and routes each interaction to the correct business operation based on the key pressed.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
paragraphs.description: This paragraph processes the administrator's Enter key action on the user list screen, identifying which user was selected and what action was requested (update or delete), then either transferring control to the appropriate maintenance program or displaying a validation error if the selection code is invalid. It also handles an optional User ID search to reposition the displayed list from a specific user onward.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PF7-KEY
paragraphs.description: Handles the administrator's request to navigate to the previous page of the user list. If already on the first page, it blocks backward navigation and informs the administrator; otherwise, it retrieves and displays the preceding page of users.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PF8-KEY
paragraphs.description: Handles the administrator's request to advance to the next page of users when PF8 is pressed. It validates that a further page of users exists before navigating forward, or informs the administrator they have already reached the last page.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph advances the user list to the next page, retrieving up to 10 user accounts from the User Security file starting from the position after the last user shown on the current page. It updates the page counter, determines whether a further page of users exists, and refreshes the screen with the new set of user records.

paragraphs.name: PROCESS-PAGE-BACKWARD
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles backward pagination through the user list, repositioning the display to show the previous page of up to 10 system users. It navigates the User Security file in reverse order, assembles the prior page of user records, adjusts the current page number accordingly, and refreshes the screen for the administrator.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-USER-DATA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph slots a single user account's details into the correct numbered row on the administrator's screen, based on which position (1–10) in the current page that user occupies. It also records the first and last user IDs on the page to support backward and forward pagination respectively.

paragraphs.name: INITIALIZE-USER-DATA
paragraphs.description: This paragraph clears a specific row in the on-screen user list, identified by its position number (1 through 10), blanking out the user ID, first name, last name, and account type fields for that row. It ensures that stale or leftover user data from a previous page is not displayed to the administrator when a new page is being built.

paragraphs.name: RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph handles the exit navigation from the User List screen, transferring the administrator back to either the sign-on screen or the previously established destination screen. It ensures that leaving this program always routes the user to an appropriate and safe screen within the CardDemo application.

paragraphs.name: SEND-USRLST-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph renders the paginated user list screen to the administrator's terminal, first assembling the screen header information and any status or error messages, then displaying the full user list either with a full screen refresh or an overlay update depending on the display mode required.

paragraphs.name: RECEIVE-USRLST-SCREEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph captures the administrator's input from the user list screen, reading any selection codes, navigation requests, or search criteria entered before the program proceeds to process the administrator's intended action.

paragraphs.name: POPULATE-HEADER-INFO
paragraphs.description: This paragraph prepares the screen header area with current date, time, and application identification details before displaying the user list to the administrator. It ensures every screen presented to the administrator is clearly stamped with the application title, program identity, and the exact moment the screen was generated.

paragraphs.name: STARTBR-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph initiates a browsing session on the User Security file, positioning the file cursor at a specific User ID so that the system can begin reading user records from that point forward for paginated display. It handles cases where the requested starting user is not found or the file is unavailable, informing the administrator accordingly.

paragraphs.name: READNEXT-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph advances sequentially through the User Security file to retrieve the next registered user account in alphabetical order by User ID. It handles end-of-file and error conditions to ensure the administrator is informed when no further users exist or when the file cannot be read.

paragraphs.name: READPREV-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph retrieves the previous user account record from the User Security file, enabling backward pagination through the list of system users. It handles boundary conditions by notifying the administrator when the beginning of the user list has been reached, or surfacing an error if the file lookup fails unexpectedly.

paragraphs.name: ENDBR-USER-SEC-FILE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formally closes the sequential browse session against the User Security file once all required user records have been retrieved for the current page. It signals to the system that no further user account lookups are needed, releasing the file browse resources cleanly.
